answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by forcing every identity to lock a refundable stake in a shared vault before it may trade, so spawning thousands of fake accounts costs real money instead of being free. Reputation then accrues slowly, like cargo passing through a single jetty: an agent that cheats forfeits its stake and its history, so it must anchor trust over time rather than buy it in bulk. Cheap identities stay worthless, proven ones earn access.
